title: Hook a laryngoscope blade onto its handle and swing it out until the light comes on
instruction: Pick up the blue blade from the yellow card and hook it onto the orange laryngoscope handle until the light comes on, then let go.
context: The manufacturer instructions for use (Medline laryngoscope IFU) tell the user to test the light before every use, so anyone who prepares an airway kit performs this check. Routine equipment check, not an emergency: for hook-on (ISO 7376 style) fibre-optic laryngoscopes the instructions tell the user to engage the blade's hook on the handle's hinge pin with 1/4 to 1 lb (1.1-4.4 N) of force, raise the blade to its operating position (about 90 deg to the handle) and check that the light comes on. A spring-loaded ball snaps over a step at the operating angle and holds the blade there against the lamp-switch spring: you hear and feel the click. ISO 7376 hook-on fittings use a hinge pin about 4 mm in diameter with a matching slot in the blade; the 4.6 mm slot and 4.0 mm pin here are class-typical dimensions. Macintosh 3 class blade, penlight-class handle.
setup: World frame: x forward from the arm-base line, y left, z up; arm bases at (0, +-0.305) m; table top z 0.7475 m. Instrument tray (stainless, light grey, 260 x 380 x 20 mm, 1.5 mm walls) centred (0.250, -0.085). On its floor a printed closed cradle (grey PLA, 5 mm wide, 9 mm high): a 108 mm rail along the handle's far side, 13.65 mm from the barrel axis; a 114 mm blade-side rail (handle frame x -139 to -25 mm), clear of the blade's swing; a 27 mm wide rear end stop whose centre is 6 mm behind the barrel end; and a 12 mm high front post (3 x 9 mm) just ahead of the head cheeks. Together they stop the handle moving in +x and turning, so no human hand is needed in a real trial. ORANGE hook-on laryngoscope handle (orange paint, painted for visibility, real handles are chrome or black; 18.3 mm OD knurled barrel, 149 mm long overall, 0.18 kg) lies in the cradle along x, head toward +x: the head has a 4 mm steel hinge pin standing upright between two cheeks, a lamp switch plunger (1 mm proud, 4000 N/m spring) in the head's stop face, and a spring plunger (M4-M5 steel spring plunger class, end force 10-40 N) whose 1.5 mm ball presses down on the blade heel. On real ISO 7376 fittings the spring balls sit in the blade and the detents on the handle; here the ball is on the handle head (equivalent kinematics). Macintosh-3-class blade (stainless, 142 mm long overall, 75 g, painted blue overall, 16 mm wide, 12 mm high heel block, 12 mm wide 18 mm tall flange, hook slot 4.6 mm wide on the 4.0 mm pin; heel back end 12 mm behind the slot bottom, slot mouth only a 1.5 mm per side chamfer over 3 mm) lies on its side on a yellow printed carrier card (190 x 50 mm, a flat marking, nothing collides with it) on the tray floor beside the handle, its blade origin (slot bottom) at (0.300, -0.175), pointing toward -x. The heel's -t prong carries an engage chamfer along its outer edge, a flat and a 1 mm step down (the lock). Pin axis at (0.300, -0.100), 16.5 mm from the barrel axis along y. Exact poses are the constants in task.py; the setup image shows the start.
scoring: Measured at the end of the episode (or at the run limit); angles from the folded position (blade along the handle). 0.25: blade hooked: the pin (4 mm) is in the blade's 4.6 mm hook slot, 2 mm or more past the end of the 3 mm mouth chamfer and no more than 0.7 mm beyond the slot bottom, within 1 mm of the slot's centreline and within 4 mm of mid-height of the heel; with a ruler this means the distance from the heel's back end to the pin axis is between 5 and 13 mm; the blade lies on its side, its vertical axis within 10 deg of the pin axis; the handle's lowest point within 10 mm of the tray floor, and no gripper centre (tool centre point) within 30 mm of the blade. 0.5: hooked as above and swung out 60 deg or more. 1.0: hooked, swung to 85 to 95 deg, lamp switch pressed in 0.4 mm or more (lamp lit, visible at the blade's light outlet), the latch crossed (while hooked and turning through 60 to 89 deg the detent plunger was pushed in at least 0.3 mm over the 80-84 deg crest, i.e. the ball climbed the engage chamfer; counts if a 20 Hz sample is in that crest band or the opening swing crosses 80-84 deg between consecutive steps) and seated at the end (ball behind the 1 mm step, plunger travel under 0.3 mm), handle and blade wholly inside the tray outline and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), both grippers open at least 30 mm and their centres at least 50 mm from blade and handle, all for 1 s (20 control steps). The lamp-switch spring pushes the blade back off 90 deg and floor friction (0.25 static, 0.20 dynamic) cannot hold it, so only the step does. Real-world judging: protractor for the angle, the lamp seen lit, you hear and feel the click, ruler for clearances and the 5 to 13 mm hooked check, stopwatch for the 1 s; after the hold, a disclosed lift probe: a gentle push back on the blade tip below HOLD_N must not move it. The swing needs ENGAGE_N at the blade tip (Medline IFU 1.1-4.4 N), the ball rides CREST_MM up the chamfer, and the lock holds with HOLD_N. 0 for the whole episode, whatever follows: the handle or blade leaves the table; the blade is bent or gouged (real-trial rule; the simulator uses the pin pushed more than 1 mm into the blade steel as its proxy). Anything else scores 0.
fidelity: Simulated by contact and springs, no scripted forces: hook slot 4.6 mm on 4.0 mm pin (small 1.5 mm chamfer), detent modelled as a hinge spring torque derived from the plunger geometry (K 15000 N/m, ball r 1.5 mm, crest 80-84 deg, seat 90 deg; 1.1-4.4 N at the blade tip), pin retained by a revolute once the slot is seated, 2000 N/m lamp switch, closed cradle. Visual only: glow patch teleported to the light outlet, yellow card, plunger ball on the handle. Painted colours for visibility.
reset_notes: Lay the handle in the closed cradle and the blade on its side as in the setup image; check the lamp switch stands 1 mm proud of the stop face and moves freely, and the detent plunger moves freely and its ball rests on the heel.
